title: Word Family Tree
intro: decide, decision, decisive, decisively — one root, four branches. Match each form to what it actually does in a sentence.

A2.why: Happy is an adjective: a happy family.
-ness turns an adjective into a noun: happy, happiness.
Quick is an adjective: a quick lunch.
-ly turns an adjective into an adverb: she walked quickly.
-ful makes an adjective: be careful on the stairs.

A2.right: adverb (with great attention, to avoid mistakes or danger)
A2.why: Add -ly to careful for the adverb: drive carefully.
Friend is a person, so it's a noun.
Careful: friendly ends in -ly but is an adjective, not an adverb. A friendly smile.

A2.right: verb (to make something easier for someone)
A2.why: Help can also be a noun (thanks for your help), but here we mean the verb: can you help me?
-ful makes an adjective: a helpful neighbour.
Beauty is the noun: the beauty of the Albufera.
-ful makes an adjective: a beautiful beach.

B1.why: Decide is the verb: we decided to stay in Valencia.
-sion makes a noun: a difficult decision.
-ive makes an adjective: a decisive leader.
Create is the verb: Sorolla created over 2,000 paintings.
-ive makes an adjective: a creative cook.
-ity makes a noun: creativity in the kitchen.
Succeed is the verb: she succeeded in passing the exam.
Success is the noun. The adjective is successful.

B1.right: verb (to give someone a paid job)
B1.why: Employ is the verb: the ranch employed twenty cowboys.

B1.right: noun (the person or company that pays you)
B1.why: -er is the one who gives the job: the employer.

B1.right: noun (a person who works for someone)
B1.why: -ee is the one who receives the job: the employee.
un- makes it negative: unemployed means without a job.

B2.why: Analyse is the verb, with -se in British English.
Analysis is the noun, plural analyses: a detailed analysis of the results.
-ical makes an adjective: an analytical mind.
A critic is a person: a film critic. Not a criticism!
Criticise is the verb, with -ise in British English.
Critical can mean finding fault (a critical review) or extremely important (a critical decision), and in hospital “in a critical condition” means dangerously ill.

B2.right: noun (a country's system of trade and money)
B2.why: Economy is the noun: the Spanish economy.
Economic means about the economy: an economic crisis.
Economical means it saves money: an economical car. Economic is about the economy.

B2.right: noun (an expert who studies the economy)

B2.why: Medicine is the noun: take your medicine after meals.
-al makes an adjective: medical school, a medical check-up.

C1.why: Persuade is the verb: she persuaded him to see a doctor.
-ive makes an adjective: a persuasive argument.
-sion makes a noun: the art of persuasion.
Ambiguous is the adjective: an ambiguous answer.
-ity makes a noun: the ambiguity of the contract.
Significant is the adjective: a significant discovery.
-ance makes a noun: the significance of Fleming's discovery.
Signify is the verb: a red flag signified danger.
-ly makes the adverb: she argued persuasively.
in- makes it negative: an insignificant amount.
Controversy is the noun: the bullfighting controversy.
-ial makes an adjective: a controversial decision.
